data.title: RBI revises forex derivative rules: What changes for transactions, cancelled contracts
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on October 10 announced regulatory measures for the foreign exchange market, including restrictions on rebooking cancelled foreign exchange derivative contracts, a reduction in transaction thresholds and the introduction of a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR).

The measures were announced through two circulars, A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 25 and A.P. (DIR Series) Circular No. 26, with the stated objective of ensuring the orderly functioning of the foreign exchange market.

Restrictions on rebooking cancelled contracts

Authorised dealers will not be permitted to allow users to rebook any foreign exchange derivative contract involving the Indian rupee, whether deliverable or non-deliverable, if it has been cancelled with any authorised dealer after the issuance of the directions.

Rollover of foreign exchange derivative contracts on maturity will continue to be permitted, subject to existing regulatory provisions.

Threshold reduced to $5 million

The RBI has reduced the threshold for undertaking foreign exchange derivative transactions to hedge contracted exposures without establishing the existence of the underlying exposure from $100 million to $5 million equivalent across all authorised dealers.

The corresponding threshold for taking positions in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee, without establishing the existence of underlying exposure, has also been reduced from $100 million to $5 million equivalent across all recognised stock exchanges taken together.

Additional documentation requirement

Authorised dealers will be required to obtain and retain an undertaking from users entering into rupee-involving foreign exchange derivative contracts to hedge contracted exposures. The undertaking must confirm that the same underlying exposure has not been hedged with any other authorised dealer.

Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve introduced

The RBI has introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve requirement for rupee-involving foreign exchange derivative contracts with a notional value exceeding $2 million equivalent.

Authorised dealers will be required to maintain a cash reserve with the RBI equal to 20% of the rupee equivalent of the notional amount of each such transaction.

The reserve requirement will apply to rupee-involving foreign exchange derivative contracts undertaken to hedge current account exposures where the user purchases foreign currency against the rupee.

The RBI said the measures are intended to strengthen market discipline, ensure appropriate risk management and maintain an orderly and transparent foreign exchange market.

data.title: Trump Announces Deal With Putin, Says Russia Will Supply Diesel To US — 'Lower Prices For Americans... Is My Greatest Priority'
data.description:
Key points:
  • Trump said Russia will initially supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the U.S. and global marketplace, followed by another 500,000 tons in November and a million tons immediately thereafter.
  • He said the potential supply could grow substantially further depending on the condition of Russia’s diesel refineries.
  • According to Trump, Russia could ultimately deliver an additional three million tons of diesel fuel “within a short period of time.”

President Donald Trump said Saturday that he reached a “highly successful” agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin that could bring a major new supply of diesel fuel to global markets as the administration looks to push energy prices lower.

Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the arrangement would involve multiple waves of Russian diesel shipments, while touting what he described as a broader effort to bring down fuel costs for Americans.

“Between our total control of the Strait of Hormuz, and this great announcement on Russian Energy, diesel prices for Americans and, indeed, the world, will be coming down, in record numbers, and fast!” he said.

Russia To Send Millions Of Tons Of Diesel, Says Trump

Trump said Russia will initially supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel fuel to the U.S. and global marketplace, followed by another 500,000 tons in November and a million tons immediately thereafter.

Trump said the potential supply could grow substantially further depending on the condition of Russia’s diesel refineries.

According to the president, Russia could ultimately deliver an additional three million tons of diesel fuel “within a short period of time.”

That would bring the total volume Trump outlined to as much as 4.8 million tons, although the timing and actual delivery of the later shipments remain dependent on refinery conditions.

“Lower prices for Americans, especially our great farmers, ranchers, and truckers, is my greatest priority. This is a very big and important announcement,” Trump added.

Trump Links Diesel Prices To Strait Of Hormuz

Trump also tied the announcement to the broader energy situation surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, saying the U.S. has “TOTAL CONTROL” of the strategic waterway.

The president argued that the combination of control over the Strait of Hormuz and additional Russian diesel supplies could put significant downward pressure on fuel prices.

The comments come as energy markets remain highly sensitive to disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz, one of the world's most important routes for global oil and fuel shipments.

Trump also added a separate warning on Iran, declaring: “Additionally, it must be understood, that Iran will not have a Nuclear Weapon!”

Crude Oil Prices Rise

Crude oil prices rose last week, with the U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) futures expiring in November rising 0.6% to $91.66 a barrel after a 1.41% fall the week before. Brent crude futures expiring in December rose 2.42% this week, hovering around $104.42 a barrel after a 3.47% increase the week before.

The United States Oil Fund ETF (USO) declined about 0.4% on Friday, while the ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil ETF (UCO) fell about 0.4%.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, was flat; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) edged up by 0.01%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) rose 0.02%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: Jewellers pitch lure of natural diamonds amid lab-grown challenge
data.description:
Bengaluru/Mumbai, Oct. 10 -- Indian jewellers are stepping up their luxury pitch for natural diamonds this festive and wedding season, playing up their rarity and lasting value as cheaper lab-grown stones vie for the same consumer cohort. With natural diamond prices under pressure, jewellers are looking to attract more buyers and create new occasions for purchases in a market that's still largely untapped.

India is the world's second-largest market for natural diamond jewellery after the US, accounting for 12% of global demand, according to De Beers, global diamond mining and jewellery giant.

The diamond market is seeing mounting pressure. De Beers' average realized rough-diamond price fell 32% to $105 a carat in the first half of 2026, while smaller, lower-quality natural stones remained under pressure from lab-grown diamonds. The miner has also paused production at its Venetia mine in South Africa for two years to cut costs, even as India remains a robust market.

In India, De Beers is trying to expand the occasions for buying natural diamonds, while widening their availability beyond large jewellery chains.

"We took a step back and said, okay, if I want to grow this market, almost create a surround sound, how would I do it?", Shweta Harit, global senior vice president of De Beers Group and chief executive Forevermark, told Mint.

De Beers is expanding diamond purchases beyond proposals and weddings, targeting occasions such as second piercings, friendship and new life stages. Its 'Love From Hubby' campaign features an empty-nester couple, while 'Love From Dad' positioned a second piercing as a new occasion for natural diamonds. "Otherwise, you're really going to be stuck at some point in proposals or maybe weddings," Harit said.

For the festive and wedding season, De Beers is positioning natural diamonds around legacy and preciousness, including a campaign with Jaipur's Maharaja Sawai Padmanabh Singh and a Forevermark campaign featuring Princess Diya Kumari. "We really believe that natural stones have aura and power," Harit said.

The push extends to retail. Forevermark had 10 stores in India by July and plans to reach 20 by the end of 2026 and 100 by 2030. De Beers has also created the Indian Natural Diamond Retailers Association, or INDRA, with the Gem & Jewellery Export Promotion Council to bring smaller jewellers into the category.

Harit said about 60% of India's jewellery market remains unorganized, with many smaller retailers having generations of experience selling gold but less familiarity with diamonds.

The low penetration leaves room for further growth, Harit said. She estimates around 12% of jewellery pieces in India contain diamonds, compared with about 70% in the US. "Typically, you start with penetration, so you start with that. Then you get into frequency, so you want to buy more often. And then, you price up," she said.

Titan partnered with designer Rahul Mishra to showcase Tanishq's latest natural diamond collection, first presented at this year's Paris Couture Week, with the collection focused on highlighting the rarity and beauty of natural diamonds.

"We were always clear that natural diamonds will have its appeal, especially in a country like India, where preciousness plays a big role," said Ajoy Chawla, managing director of Titan Co. Ltd. "People do expect their jewellery to have a certain value retention. Overall, the store of value is important."

Tanishq has rolled out diamond experience centres in about 200 stores, where customers can study natural diamonds and understand their difference from lab-grown alternatives. The company is also shifting the conversation towards sparkle and visual appeal.

Titan's studded jewellery business is showing that the strategy is translating into demand. In its June quarter earnings call on 7 August, Chawla said the product mix was "swinging upwards towards more studded scale" and called it an important driver for the jewellery division. Titan's studded jewellery grew in the mid-30s in the first quarter of fiscal year 2027 (Q1FY27), and the company said buyer growth in studded jewellery continued to outpace gold jewellery.

The momentum continued into the September quarter, with Titan reporting early-30s growth in studded jewellery in its Q2 update on 6 October, even as the overall jewellery portfolio grew 21%.

At the same time, Titan is not betting exclusively on natural diamonds. It launched beYon, its lab-grown diamond brand, in December 2025. Senco Gold and Diamonds has Sennes, while Trent has Pome under Westside, giving some of India's largest organised jewellery and retail groups a presence in both natural and lab-grown diamonds.

Lab-grown diamonds cost roughly one-tenth of a natural diamond of the same size/carat. They, however, do not have any resale value, and jewellers typically do not accept them for resale.

"You get a sense that you're not caught up in the semantics of the 4Cs," Chawla said, echoing similar marketing efforts by Indriya. "4Cs is such a dry way to describe a diamond. What matters is-what is the brilliance, the light performance, how do you see it come alive in front of you?"

To be sure, the 4Cs refer to the cut, colour, clarity and carat weight, making the global standard for evaluating diamond quality.

The bottom line, Chawla said, is that natural diamonds are one-of-a-kind, unlike each other, and not a commodity. He compared them with Indian heritage goods such as luxurious hand-woven textiles, which are valued for the slight imperfections that handmade work by master craftsmen inevitably leaves behind. In June, Indriya ran a 'Sparkle Like No Other' campaign with brand ambassador Aditi Rao Hydari to promote natural diamonds.

The challenge for the industry is that lab-grown diamonds are rapidly gaining ground. The International Gemological Institute's consolidated certification revenue from lab-grown diamond jewellery rose 44% year-on-year in April-June, while natural-diamond jewellery certification revenue grew 2%. Lab-grown loose-stone certification revenue rose 25%, compared with 6% for natural loose stones, according to IGI's investor presentation.

IGI said the lab-grown jewellery segment has seen over 1,000 retail showrooms across India as new players enter the market, while large manufacturers are adding capacity.

Indriya is taking a similar approach, moving beyond the traditional 4Cs in its natural-diamond marketing campaign launched in June this year.

"The context is that the Indian jewellery market is worth Rs.800k crores, and in that large market, about less than 10% is currently diamond jewellery. It is a very small segment of the total market at this time," said Sandeep Kohli, chief executive of Indriya.

"As jewellery progresses more towards a combo of beauty and adornment along with investment and store of value, people will want more jewellery in their drawers. If only less than 10% of Indian customers have diamond jewellery, they will want variety," Kohli said.

"There is a big market for diamond-based jewellery in India, and there will be growth. There will be people who prefer something more precious, like natural diamonds. And there will be some who may want to go for lab-grown diamonds given their budgets," he said. "If the diamond business overall is small, the LGDs business is tiny. You have to see where the market settles."

Indriya is also rolling out diamond-studded versions of most of its designs. Its upcoming Padmika collection, for instance, will be available in both gold and diamond versions.

"Besides polki (uncut diamonds), diamonds have not been part of traditional jewellery. But look at a category like mangalsutra, the share of diamond-based jewellery in that category is higher than the average diamond share of jewellery overall," said Kohli.

The shift is filtering down to smaller jewellers. "The price correction is making customers more comfortable exploring diamond jewellery across a wider range of occasions and price points," said Supriya Kataria, founder of Kumari Fine Jewellery, based in Mumbai. Demand is strongest for lightweight, design-led pieces, with some customers trading savings for larger or better-quality stones, she said.

At Zen Diamond India, also headquartered in Mumbai, lower prices are bringing in more first-time buyers and encouraging existing customers to upgrade, said managing director Neil Sonawala. He expects natural diamonds to remain the key sales driver this season.

data.title: MAG 7 Voices: How Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta Reshaped AI This Week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is pushing to bring Nvidia’s AI computing platform to personal computers and has committed $1 billion over five years to U.S. scientific research.
  • Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella sees secure desktop environments as essential for AI agents, predicting that local and cloud-based intelligence will increasingly work together.
  • Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai has emphasized Google’s integrated AI stack, while its new Gemini agent’s use of rival models highlights a more flexible approach.

The Magnificent Seven are no longer making the same bet on artificial intelligence. Microsoft (MSFT) wants them running securely on personal computers. Alphabet’s (GOOG, GOOGL) Google is building a cloud-based agent that can handle complex tasks and retain context. Meta (META) is putting its assistant into new devices, including a wearable pendant.

But the race to make AI more capable is running alongside a harder question for investors: how quickly can the technology generate durable revenue?

A Financial Times report on Thursday stated that OpenAI told prospective investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50 billion, below the roughly $68 billion figure widely reported two months earlier.

The report attributed the gap in part to different accounting methods. Anthropic includes revenue from cloud partners such as Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, while OpenAI does not.

The distinction does not necessarily indicate a sudden deterioration in demand, but it has given investors another reason to scrutinize the numbers behind the AI investment cycle. Nvidia (NVDA) underperformed the Roundhill Magnificent Seven ETF (MAGS) so far this week, while Apple (AAPL) outperformed.

Washington is also trying to shape the next phase of the industry. President Donald Trump named Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton as AI czar on Sunday to lead a “Super Intelligence Force,” which has 120 days to report.

Nvidia: Bringing The AI Stack To The Desktop

Clayton’s 120-day reporting clock is also running. For investors, the bigger question is whether the next round of AI launches can show a credible path from impressive capabilities and heavy infrastructure spending to durable revenue. OpenAI’s latest revenue disclosure has brought that question back to the center of the AI trade.

The pitch extends Nvidia’s business beyond the data centers that have driven its growth. RTX Spark laptop preorders opened Wednesday ahead of an October 16 release, and Nvidia previewed a Windows version of its GB300-based DGX Station with 748GB of memory.

Huang also tied Nvidia’s strategy to the administration’s science agenda. At a Washington event Thursday, the company committed $1 billion over five years to U.S. scientific research, quantum computing, healthcare and energy security under Trump’s Genesis Mission.

“With a $1 billion investment, NVIDIA is putting advanced Super Intelligence in the hands of America’s scientists,” Huang said, describing the effort as a way to turn “scientific leadership into industrial leadership.” The language echoes the administration’s “Super Intelligence” branding, while Nvidia continues to sell the computing systems needed to support those ambitions.

Microsoft: The Sandbox Is The Product

Microsoft made its Execution Containers generally available Wednesday, giving AI agents a restricted environment in which to operate without unrestricted access to a user’s data or ability to take actions on a device. Anthropic, OpenAI and Nvidia will use the technology.

“We needed to make the desktop the most secure place for agents to execute,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said. He added that “hybrid intelligence will be everywhere,” suggesting that local computing and cloud services will increasingly work together rather than compete as mutually exclusive options.

Hardware is only part of the story. Microsoft has guided for Windows OEM and Devices revenue to decline in the high teens in fiscal 2027, while demand for its Azure cloud service continues to exceed available supply. Moor Insights analyst Anshel Sag said the memory crunch could make local AI a purchase mainly for customers with the budget to afford it.

Alphabet: One Agent, Multiple Models

Google Cloud introduced its Gemini agent Thursday, presenting it as a single assistant for work that takes “objectives, not instructions.” The system can coordinate sub-agents on tasks that may run for hours or days. It remains in private preview, with broader availability across Workspace expected later.

A notable feature is its ability to select the model best suited to a task. The agent currently uses both Google’s Gemini and Anthropic’s Claude models.

Wall Street is watching the hardware behind that strategy. Wells Fargo raised its price target on Alphabet to $417 from $411 and projected external sales of its tensor processing units (TPUs) at $9.2 billion in the third quarter (Q3) and $11.5 billion in the fourth quarter (Q4). Those estimates include hardware installed in customers’ own data centers.

Meta: Free AI, Unanswered Questions

Meta is taking a different approach by distributing its AI assistant through consumer devices. Muse is free for now while Meta explores its options, and IDC analyst Meredith Whalen said “the real question is trust.”

Microsoft may help Meta expand the assistant’s reach. Microsoft’s announcement said Muse will integrate with its execution containers and receive a native Windows app, although no release date, pricing or user target was provided.

Amazon: Making The Case For $220 Billion In Spending

Amazon’s (AMZN) AI spending drew attention through comments from AWS CEO Matt Garman on the a16z podcast Thursday. Garman said AWS’s largest customer accounts for only a single-digit share of revenue and put Amazon’s 2026 capital expenditure near $220 billion. He also noted that startups contribute 30% to 40% of AWS revenue, with Trainium capacity sold out for the next year.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos offered a more personal view of AI’s potential in an interview with Fox News. He said AI could allow some people to decide, “I can support my family working three days a week,” and promoted Prometheus, the startup he co-leads.

Apple: Cook Steps Back, Ternus Faces The AI Test

Apple’s week was defined by the transition from Tim Cook to John Ternus. In an interview with The Independent, Cook said he stepped down on September 1 partly to give Ternus “some wind at his back.” He also called the iPhone Duo amazing, while Ternus remained largely out of the spotlight.

Apple has confirmed a second fall event for Octo ber. 13. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman expects the company to introduce a smart-home hub with a screen, a new HomePod mini and an updated Apple TV, all built around Siri AI.

Tesla: Terafab Takes A New Turn

Tesla’s (TSLA) AI plans also shifted during the week. CEO Elon Musk confirmed Saturday that talks with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSM) about the Terafab chip complex were “just discussions, but something may come of it.” By Wednesday, Musk said Tesla and his other companies would build and operate Terafab themselves, with TSMC potentially limited to subleasing space.

Musk also accused unnamed “oligarchs” in India of blocking Starlink’s launch to protect a “monopolistic chokehold” on connectivity, according to comments reported Wednesday.

Tesla’s robotaxi operations continued to expand. Service hours in Austin moved to 11 p.m., with Musk explaining the limit as “literally trying to avoid grey kittens on grey tarmac in the dark.” Round-the-clock service is tied to the planned release of FSD v15 this month.

Texas records reportedly show Cybercab registrations at 319, up from 169, although Austin remains the only public robotaxi market. Tesla also faces an October 30 deadline to provide the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration with sworn answers about Cybercab safety certification.

The operating numbers offered a brighter spot. Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, beating the 461,974 consensus estimate by 5.3%. Energy-storage deployments totaled 13.7 gigawatt-hours, below the 15.9 GWh estimate. Tesla reports earnings on October 21.

What To Watch

Slated for next week is Apple’s event on Tuesday. Tesla’s Roadster demonstration is scheduled for Thursday, followed by the October 16 start of RTX Spark laptop shipments and Surface Laptop Ultra deliveries.

Clayton’s 120-day reporting clock is also running. For investors, the bigger question is whether the next round of AI launches can show a credible path from impressive capabilities and heavy infrastructure spending to durable revenue.

data.title: India central bank takes steps to support rupee, opens dollar window for oil companies
data.description:
India's central bank has announced more measures to support the rupee on Saturday after the currency fell to within striking distance of its record low.

  • The Reserve Bank of India will open a special window to meet the daily dollar requirements of three government oil-marketing companies to ease the pressure on the spot market

  • Under such an arrangement, used in times of strain on the currency, the RBI provides oil companies dollars directly from its foreign exchange reserves

  • Indian Oil , Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum will be allowed to access to access dollars under the facility from Monday, the RBI said

  • Forex dealers will not spermit users to rebook any foreign exchange derivatives, the bank said

  • The RBI slashed the limit for positions in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee to $5 million from $100 million

  • The central bank asked forex dealers to maintain a "foreign exchange risk reserve" for all derivative contracts involving the rupee equal to 20% of the notional amount of each transaction

  • The RBI has raised dollars and hiked its policy rate, but pressure on the currency has persisted. On Friday, the rupee closed at 96.73 per dollar, barely changed from its previous close, and near its all-time weakest level of 96.96, hit in May

data.title: RBI announces special dollar window for three PSU oil companies from October 12
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced a special window to meet the entire daily dollar requirements of three public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs), effective October 12, 2026.

The facility will cover Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL), Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), the central bank said in a press release dated October 10.

Under the arrangement, the RBI will sell US dollars to the three companies through designated banks. The facility will remain in place until further notice.

The central bank said the decision was taken after assessing current market conditions.

The move comes as the rupee remains under pressure, having traded at record-low levels in recent sessions.

On Friday, October 9, the domestic currency appreciated 17 paise to close at 96.71 against the US dollar, recovering from Thursday's (October 8's) close of 96.88.

Forex traders attributed Friday's recovery to a softer US dollar, easing crude oil prices and likely intervention by the central bank.

Oil marketing companies require dollars to pay for crude oil imports. The special window will provide a dedicated channel for meeting the entire daily dollar requirements of the three public sector companies, according to the RBI's announcement.

The central bank did not specify the pricing mechanism for the dollar sales or the volume of foreign exchange expected to be supplied under the facility.

data.title: Zetwerk eyes Rs.27,000 crore IPO valuation as over 30 investors weigh anchor book
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Zetwerk, a business-to-business (B2B) manufacturing platform, is preparing to tap the public markets as it seeks to capitalise on growing investor interest in India's industrial growth story.

The company is looking to launch its initial public offering (IPO) in the next few weeks at a valuation of around Rs.27,000 crore ($3.1 billion), according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The IPO is expected to comprise a fresh issue of Rs.2,830 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of Rs.2,200 crore by existing investors.

Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA), Norway's central bank, and the asset management arms of Goldman Sachs, SBI and HDFC are among more than 30 foreign and domestic investors considering participation in Zetwerk's anchor book ahead of its IPO, said the first of the two persons cited earlier, both speaking on condition of anonymity.

"There is a diversified book that includes mutual funds and key FIIs. The company is likely to be valued at around Rs.27,000 crore," said the second person, adding that more investors would be added to the anchor book by Sunday night.

The company said it would announce the price band of the IPO on Monday, 12 October.

Other marquee investors that have expressed interest in the anchor book include SBI Pension Fund, BlackRock, Edelweiss Asset Management and Norges Bank, Norway's central bank.

The company is expected to file its red herring prospectus (RHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) within the next two weeks. the people said.

Norges Bank and SBI Pension Fund said they had no comments, while Abu Dhabi Investment Authority declined to comment. Zetwerk did not immediately respond to Mint's email seeking comment. Mint also reached out to SBI Mutual Fund, HDFC AMC, Edelweiss AMC, Goldman Sachs AMC, and BlackRock for comment but did not receive a responses by press time.

Founded in 2018 by Amrit Acharya, Srinath Ramakkrushnan, Vishal Chaudhary, Ankit Fatehpuria and Rahul Sharma, Zetwerk runs on its proprietary software platform, Zetwerk OS, which manages sourcing, production planning, supplier coordination and project execution. The company operates through its own facilities and a network of third-party manufacturers, supplying products to a wide range of sectors, including utilities, renewable energy, consumer electronics, artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, space and defence, oil and gas, industrial automation and aerospace, both in India and overseas.

Zetwerk recorded an estimated operating revenue of Rs.15,900 crore in fiscal year 2026 (FY26), up 24% from fiscal year 2025 (FY25), Inc42 reported in June, citing a rating rationale from Crisil Ratings.

Zetwerk is preparing to enter the public markets at a time when investor sentiment remains subdued, particularly towards technology stocks. The Nifty IT index has fallen 24% so far in 2026, significantly underperforming the benchmark Nifty 50, which has declined 14%. The weak market sentiment could make investor demand and pricing key determinants of the success of Zetwerk's IPO, market participants said.

In an October report, Axis Direct said that "the IT Services is likely to report relatively moderate earnings growth (in Q2FY27), as global demand remains cautious."

However, ramp-ups in large deals, outcome-based engagements and rising AI-led spending should lend some support. Margins are expected to remain mixed, with wage hikes, AI investments, deal ramp-up costs and acquisitions weighing on profitability, partly offset by rupee depreciation and productivity gains, the brokerage added.

Since its founding, Zetwerk has raised a total of $931 million across 20 funding rounds as of 27 September, according to Tracxn data, with the last round raised early this year valuing it at $4 billion. Zetwerk is backed by investors including Greenoaks Capital, Khosla Ventures, Accel, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Peak XV Partners, Avenir Growth Capital, and Baillie Gifford.

The Bengaluru-based company has appointed Kotak Mahindra Capital, JM Financial, Avendus Capital, Pantomath Capital, and the Indian arms of HSBC, Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs as merchant bankers for its IPO.

Recent technology listings have seen mixed fortunes. ArMee Infotech, which listed on 30 September, opened flat but ended its debut session 21% lower. Fractal Analytics listed at a nearly 3% discount to its issue price on 16 February and closed the day down about 6%. In contrast, ESDS Software Solution made a strong debut on 4 September, listing at a premium of more than 76% and ending its first trading day up 109%.

Zetwerk's clients span a range of industries, from industrial heavyweights such as L&T, NTPC and Indian Oil to consumer electronics brand boAt and global companies such as Siemens, Acer and Schneider Electric. Other clients include National Aluminium Company Ltd (Nalco), CG Power Solutions, Nordex, Bharat Bijlee and Mortenson.

data.title: Stronger BoP outlook to keep Rupee far more stable; FY27 surplus seen at USD 97-100 billion: Report
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- India's external position exhibits significant resilience as a robust balance of payments (BoP) projection provides substantial support to the domestic currency, according to a research report by ICICI Bank. The report projected that the country's BoP surplus will expand sharply to reach between USD 97 billion and USD 100 billion in the financial year 2026-27 (FY27).

The research findings attribute this positive trajectory to steady capital receipts, manageable trade parameters, and expanding external reserves, which together create a protective cushion against global macroeconomic volatility and spillover risks.

In its macroeconomic evaluation, the ICICI Bank research report said: "A bigger change is the far more stable performance of the domestic currency compared with the sharper depreciation episodes seen earlier in the year."

On the current account front, higher remittances up 24 per cent year-on-year in the April-July period and steady services export growth of 8.5 per cent year-on-year in the April-August period cushion the goods deficit.

With average crude oil prices near USD 94 per barrel, the merchandise goods deficit is projected at USD 387 billion to USD 400 billion, keeping the current account deficit between 1.2 per cent and 1.6 per cent of gross domestic product.

"Overall, we see BoP surplus of USD 97-100bn in FY27 now compared with a large deficit seen in last two years," the report said.

Macroeconomic growth remains firm, expanding by 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of FY27, supported by exports, investments, and manufacturing activity. Overall annual economic growth is estimated at 7.1 per cent. Headline inflation faces upward pressure from lower monsoon rainfall and sowing deficits, bringing expected inflation to 5.0 per cent and prompting potential policy tightening.

"In the near-term, the stronger dollar profile and higher oil prices could continue to keep the INR under pressures, but RBI's active dollar selling should ensure a much stable trading environment for the domestic currency," the report noted.

"Given the large FX inflows and stronger FX reserves (USD 780bn), the central bank is in a much better position to curb the excessive depreciation pressures unlike earlier periods," the report added.

The central bank holds a forward dollar book of USD 137 billion as of July-end. On a 40-currency real effective exchange rate basis, the Indian currency remains undervalued, with USD/INR projected to trade within a range of 94 to 96 in the near term.

data.title: Isaias weakens to Category 1 hurricane after Florida landfall, NHC says
data.description:
Hurricane Isaias rapidly lost windspeed on Friday, weakening into a Category 1 event after making landfall near Destin, Florida, the US National Hurricane Center said, but warned of danger from storm surges and floods as power links snapped.

The hurricane was about 65 miles (105 km) west-northwest of Panama City, Florida, packing maximum sustained winds of 90 mph (150 kph), the NHC said in its most recent advisory.

Earlier this week, Donald Trump established a "committee of inquiry" to investigate whether Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook made false statements on mortgage documents, setting a Nov. 5 hearing on the allegations.

Lisa Cook Can Present Evidence at Hearing

Trump’s memo says Cook should appear and can present arguments, written evidence and witness statements.

data.title: Indian Navy to Commission Indigenous ASW Shallow Water Craft
data.description:
Build by Cochin Shipyard in Kochi, the Anti-Submarine Warfare Vessel Commissions at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai

Mangrol, the third Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC) built by Cochin Shipyard (CSL), Kochi, is set to be commissioned into the Indian Navy on 12 Oct 2026 at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. The ceremony will be presided over by Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Western Naval Command. The event will be attended by senior naval and defence officials, representatives from the Ministry of Defence and Cochin Shipyard, veterans and representatives of indigenous weapons and sensor manufacturers.

Named after Mangrol, a coastal town and prominent fishing harbour in Gujarat's Junagadh district, the ship carries forward the legacy of the erstwhile INS Mangrol (M85), a minesweeper that served the Indian Navy until 07 Apr 2004. The naming of the ship continues the Navy's tradition of preserving the legacy of its former warships.

Built with over 80% indigenous content, Mangrol reflects India's growing capabilities in warship design, construction and integration of advanced weapons and sensors. Constructed by CSL under the Government of India’s Make in India and Aatmanirbhar Bharat initiatives, the ship marks another important step towards self-reliance in defence shipbuilding.

Designed to detect and counter underwater threats in coastal and shallow waters, Mangrol is equipped with modern weapons and sensors, including the Abhay Hull-Mounted Sonar, lightweight torpedoes, an indigenous anti-submarine rocket launcher and the Maareech Advanced Torpedo Decoy System. Powered by three diesel engines with waterjet propulsion, the ship offers high manoeuvrability for operations in shallow waters. It is also capable of undertaking underwater surveillance, Low-Intensity Maritime Operations and mine warfare-related tasks.

Mangrol will strengthen the Indian Navy's anti-submarine warfare capabilities, particularly in coastal waters where larger warships face operational limitations. The ship can operate alongside maritime patrol aircraft, helicopters and other warships to detect and counter submarine threats. Its induction will enhance the Navy's ability to protect ports, harbours and coastal approaches while supporting wider fleet operations.

Amid growing underwater threats in the evolving maritime security environment, the commissioning of Mangrol marks an important milestone in strengthening the Indian Navy's anti-submarine warfare capabilities, particularly in coastal waters.

data.title: Wellness-Washing At Work: Do Corporate Mental Health Programmes Deliver?
data.description:
Employers count logins and webinar seats, but trust, workload and managers decide whether anyone is actually helped

On World Mental Health Day, observed on 10 October, many Indian employers can point to a helpline, a wellbeing app and a calendar of webinars. Far fewer can demonstrate that these initiatives have left employees better supported. That gap between what companies offer and what employees experience gives this year's theme, ‘Lived Experiences Heard: Real Voices, Real Change’, its sharpest workplace test. It is also where the charge of wellness-washing — a tick-box approach that looks caring without changing much — begins.

The case for action is clear. The World Health Organization (WHO) and the International Labour Organization (ILO) estimate that 12 billion workdays are lost every year to depression and anxiety, costing the global economy nearly USD 1 trillion.

They also estimate that 15 per cent of working-age adults live with a mental disorder. India's gap between need and care is wider still: a post on the community platform of the National Association of Software and Service Companies (Nasscom) cites the National Mental Health Survey (2016) in putting the treatment gap for common mental disorders at more than 85 per cent.

For Arindam Chakraborty, Chief Human Resources Officer at Saatvik Green Energy, that scale makes mental health a business question. "With an estimated 12 billion working days lost globally each year to depression and anxiety, organisations need to view mental health as a business and people priority, not simply a benefits metric," he said.

The senior people leaders who responded to BW People's questions agree on the premise but are candid about its limits. Set against the research, their answers point to an uncomfortable conclusion: the measures employers report most readily are often the ones that reveal the least about whether employees are better supported.

The Number Everyone Counts

Usage is the figure employers can report most easily, and Titan Company's figures are substantial. Adoption of Maithri, the company's employee support programme, grew from 18 per cent to 31 per cent last year, while its floor-walk initiatives recorded more than 4,300 touchpoints. Yet Titan's leadership treats those numbers as a beginning rather than a result.

"Usage numbers are an important starting point, but they don’t tell us the whole story," said Priya Mathilakath Pillai, Chief People Officer at Titan Company. "However, participation alone doesn’t establish effectiveness," she added.

The World Economic Forum (WEF) makes a similar point in its February 2024 report, ‘Measuring What Matters: Assessing Workplace Mental Health and Well-being’, led by Richard Heron and Ruma Bharava. The report advises employers against treating participation rates, health-check data and similar figures as evidence of lasting improvement. It also notes that workplace screening has not been shown to reduce symptoms or improve productivity, and cites early findings from the Mental Health at Work Index suggesting that only one in four organisations has a mental health strategy.

Titan does not claim to have closed that gap. "Our red-flag SOPs support early identification and intervention, though we recognise that measuring long-term impact remains a work in progress," Pillai said.

What Employees Are Really Asking

The leaders agree that stigma remains a barrier, but it is not the only one. Employees, Pillai said, are essentially asking themselves three questions: "Is it safe? Is it confidential? Is it worth my time?"

Confidentiality and concerns about managers' perceptions can weigh as heavily as stigma, and sometimes more. "Employees may hesitate if seeking help could affect how they are perceived or influence performance evaluations and future opportunities," Pillai said.

"While stigma remains a significant barrier, concerns around confidentiality and how managers may perceive employees seeking help can be equally important," said Remya Thomas, Group HR Head at Embassy Services.

Survey data from India points in the same direction. In ‘Naukri Pulse 2025’, a survey of 19,650 jobseekers across 80 industries released by job portal Naukri on 10 October 2025, nearly three in four respondents said they hesitated to be open about taking time off for mental health reasons. Some 45 per cent would record it as general sick leave, 19 per cent would rather not take leave at all and 9 per cent would give a different excuse.

The most common fear, cited by 31 per cent, was being seen as incapable, while 21 per cent feared an impact on career growth. Among respondents with up to five years of experience, only around 25 per cent would identify a mental health day as such, compared with 43 per cent who would record it as sick leave.

For Chakraborty, availability is not the same as safety. "Recent research found that while 75% of employees said their supervisors were consistently available and responsive, only 41% felt comfortable discussing mental health concerns with managers or HR. This gap shows that accessibility alone is insufficient; psychological safety and credible confidentiality are what build trust," he said.

Programme design is another factor. "If access is difficult, responses are slow, communication is unclear, or support feels generic, employees disengage. Even the best programme cannot succeed without trust and accessibility," Pillai said. Even tools intended to detect distress can fuel concerns: the WEF report flags risks involving false positives, bias and breaches of confidentiality in workplace screening.

When Programmes Miss The Point

If trust is the barrier, adding more programmes will not necessarily remove it. Writing on the WEF platform in March 2025, Anthea Ong, Chairperson and Founder of WorkWell Leaders, cited a study of 46,000 employees in the United Kingdom that found individual support, from counselling services to mindfulness sessions, had no significant effect on overall mental wellbeing. Ong argued that such programmes often treat symptoms rather than causes and see limited take-up. She called for changes in leadership and manager behaviour, workload and work design. The article presents her views, rather than those of the WEF itself.

Indian research points to a similar gap. A review of 30 records published in Frontiers in Public Health in May 2022 by Apurvakumar Pandya, Niharika Khanal and Mudita Upadhyaya found that most workplace mental health interventions in India were curative, primarily involving counselling. Few included a needs assessment, impact evaluation or changes to workplace policy.

Employees are more direct about what would help. Asked to select the single change that would help most, 60 per cent of Naukri's respondents chose flexible work options, compared with 22 per cent for stress-management workshops, 10 per cent for paid mental health days and 9 per cent for managerial training.

The last figure highlights a difference between employee preferences and expert recommendations. The WHO's 2022 guidelines on mental health at work, supported by a joint WHO/ILO policy brief, recommend manager training alongside action on heavy workloads and negative workplace behaviours.

That is the logic behind Chakraborty's warning. "A counselling helpline, for instance, has limited value if employees continue to face excessive workloads, poor manager support or a culture where speaking about stress is seen as a weakness," he said.

"The more effective approach combines confidential access to professional support with manager training, mental health awareness, flexibility and mechanisms for employees to voice concerns safely," he added.

Where The Law Stops

One legal analysis suggests that existing legislation does little to close the gap. The four Labour Codes, including the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions (OSH) Code, 2020, came into effect on 21 November 2025, according to the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

Writing on a Wolters Kluwer legal blog three days earlier, Neha Vyas of Newcastle University argued that the OSH Code addresses physical injury but leaves psychosocial hazards out. If that interpretation holds, workplace mental health support remains largely a matter of employer choice, making the quality of that choice more consequential.

The Economic Survey 2024-25, released on 31 January 2025, also highlighted the relationship between work and mental wellbeing. As reported by Business Standard, the Survey cited research by the Sapien Labs Centre for Human Brain and Mind suggesting that people with the strongest relationships with managers and colleagues report mental wellbeing scores 100 points higher than those with the weakest relationships. It also warned that working more than 55 to 60 hours a week can seriously harm health.

The findings lend weight to what Pillai and Thomas described: how a manager responds can determine whether an employee ever uses a helpline.

What Better Looks Like

Chakraborty's test is straightforward. "The success of a workplace mental health programme should not be measured by how many employees download an app or attend a webinar, but by whether it creates a healthier and more supportive workplace," he said.

He would track employees' confidence in seeking support, psychological safety, absenteeism, retention, engagement, and the effectiveness of return-to-work and workplace accommodation measures. "Equally important is whether employees feel heard and whether managers are better equipped to recognise and respond to distress," he said.

Thomas offers a similar yardstick. Embassy Services creates regular opportunities for open conversations, mindfulness and wellbeing engagement to normalise the subject, she said, with a clear aim: "The objective should be to create an environment where seeking support is viewed as a positive step, rather than a sign of weakness."

On measurement, Thomas said, "Participation numbers offer only one part of the picture." Employers should also assess whether employees feel more comfortable discussing wellbeing, know where to seek support and have managers equipped to respond.

"For us, the measure of success is not simply how many people attend a session, but whether these initiatives help create a culture where wellbeing becomes part of everyday conversations and behaviours," she said.

Titan has layered other measures over its usage data. On its internal listening platform, Tell Me, the managing director and chief people officer spend more than 80 hours with different employee groups, while Heartbeat measures wellbeing and drives manager- and function-level action plans.

Employee feedback led Titan to extend its support programme to off-roll employees. Its wellbeing score rose by four points this year, and its campaign ‘It’s Okay to NOT be Okay’, in which senior leaders share personal experiences, was followed by higher uptake, Pillai said. The company also examines trends over time.

"Over time, trends in absenteeism, burnout, attrition and engagement can help us understand whether employees are better supported, not just whether they are using the programme," she said.

The evidence does not suggest that workplace programmes never help. Rather, it shows that employers often struggle to demonstrate their impact, that participation figures alone offer limited proof of effectiveness, and that trust, managers and workload shape outcomes.

Three tests follow: whether employees believe seeking help will remain confidential and will not count against them during performance appraisals; whether managers are trained to recognise distress and respond appropriately; and whether employers track absenteeism, attrition and the proportion of employees who say they feel heard, rather than relying on logins alone.

"My advice to companies is simple: do not ask only whether a programme exists; ask whether employees feel safer, heard and better supported because it exists," Chakraborty said.

data.title: Mental Health At Work: Are Organisations Overlooking The Wellbeing Of Managers?
data.description:
Managers are caught between business targets, employee expectations and organisational change, raising questions about whether companies are supporting the people expected to hold teams together

Managers are often positioned as the first line of support when employees struggle with workload, performance pressure or organisational change. Yet the people expected to absorb these pressures are increasingly facing their own strain. In India, manager engagement fell sharply in 2025, even as organisations continued to depend on managers to translate business priorities into everyday work.

Gallup’s ‘State of the Global Workplace 2026’ shows that engagement among Indian managers fell from 39 per cent in 2024 to 30 per cent in 2025. Engagement among individual contributors also declined, from 24 per cent to 19 per cent. Globally, manager engagement fell from 27 per cent to 22 per cent over the same period.

The decline matters because managers operate in the middle of competing expectations. They are expected to deliver business targets, manage larger or changing teams, implement new processes and technology, address employee concerns and meet senior leadership expectations, often without equivalent increases in authority, resources or time.

“Managerial stress becomes an organisational design problem when it shifts from situational to structural. When managers constantly navigate competing priorities, large teams and limited authority while remaining fully accountable, demanding resilience fails,” said Rajani Jalan, Chief Mentor – CSR and People Relations, mPokket.

The Pressure In The Middle

Gallup’s India findings point to a wider management problem. The report says Indian managers are increasingly expected to reconcile executive demands with changing employee expectations, organisational restructuring, AI adoption and tighter resources. It also notes that managers account for around 70 per cent of the variance in team engagement.

That creates a paradox. Organisations expect managers to improve the employee experience while their own ability to remain engaged depends partly on whether they have enough time, authority, support and resources to perform the role effectively. The size of a manager’s team alone does not determine whether the role becomes unsustainable. Gallup points instead to factors such as managerial capability, collaboration, time, authority, empowerment, technology, process design and organisational support.

This shifts the conversation away from individual resilience. If a manager is given responsibility for a growing team but limited decision-making power, unrealistic timelines and insufficient support, the resulting strain is not simply a question of personal coping ability.

“The practical implication is to inspect the whole job before widening a manager’s team. Review personal targets alongside team size, employee experience and the complexity of the work. If a team grows, decide which individual responsibilities can move,” said Gaurav Sharma, CHRO, True Balance.

Change Adds Another Layer

The wider workplace environment is adding to that pressure. Deloitte’s ‘2026 Global Human Capital Trends’ finds that one-third of respondents experienced 15 or more major changes during the previous year. Sixty-eight per cent reported a decline in wellbeing because of organisational change, while 60 per cent reported increased workloads. Only 27 per cent of leaders said their organisations manage change effectively.

For managers, repeated restructuring or shifting priorities can create a particularly difficult position. They have to communicate changes they may not have designed, maintain team performance while roles are changing and manage uncertainty among employees, while continuing to meet their own targets.

“Resilience is important, but it works best when enabled by thoughtful organisational design. Clear roles, realistic priorities, flexibility and appropriate decision-making authority allow managers to focus their energy where it matters. The organisation’s role is to create an environment where sustained performance and individual wellbeing can coexist,” said Bhavya Misra, Chief Human Resource Officer, Godrej Capital.

The International Labour Organization’s 2026 report on the psychosocial working environment reinforces the structural nature of the issue. It identifies workload, long working hours, job insecurity, high demands with low control, role clarity and workplace harassment among the factors that shape psychosocial risk. The ILO estimates that psychosocial risk factors are linked to more than 840,000 deaths annually and nearly 45 million disability-adjusted life years lost each year.

The figures are global and do not specifically measure managers. But they underline why the design and management of work cannot be separated from worker wellbeing.

When Pressure Becomes Personal

The consequences of sustained workplace pressure can become more serious than disengagement or exhaustion. In July 2025, Shivshankar Mitra, a chief manager at Bank of Baroda’s Baramati branch, died by suicide at the workplace. A note recovered by police cited work pressure. Mitra had submitted his resignation days earlier, citing health concerns and work pressure, and was serving his notice period.

Another case emerged in Bengaluru in March 2025, involving Vivek Samdarshi, a Regional Head of Sales at ICICI Bank. His family alleged that he had faced sustained humiliation and pressure from senior officials, and a police complaint was filed. Police registered a case and investigated the allegations.

These cases should not be presented as proof that workplace pressure alone caused the deaths. Suicide is complex and can involve multiple personal, social and psychological factors. In Samdarshi’s case, the allegations against senior officials were made by his family and were subject to investigation. The cases nevertheless raise a difficult question for employers: what happens when a manager who is already under severe pressure remains responsible for delivering targets, managing people and navigating organisational demands?

A third case also illustrates why causation needs caution. In January 2026, Indian Oil Corporation Executive Director Ajay Garg died by suicide in Noida. Police recovered a note, but reports said it did not name anyone or establish a reason. Seniority, therefore, cannot be treated as evidence of immunity from mental-health distress, nor can workplace pressure automatically be assumed to be the cause.

“The starting point is an inclusive culture where people feel safe speaking up without fear of judgement. Leaders should be sensitised to recognise changes in behaviour, respond with empathy and connect colleagues with appropriate professional support,” said Misra.

Support Must Reach Managers

The response cannot stop at Employee Assistance Programmes or occasional wellbeing sessions. Those measures may have value, but they do not address an overloaded team structure, unclear authority or unrealistic performance expectations.

Organisations need to examine managerial spans of control, workload allocation, staffing, decision-making authority and the frequency with which priorities change. Managers also need channels where they can raise concerns without being perceived as unable to cope.

What Organisations Can Do To Protect Managers’ Mental Health

“Every new template, calibration exercise, survey action plan and learning requirement asks managers for time. The combined demand still needs an owner. For each new requirement, HR should be able to explain the work it creates, the decision it improves and the task it replaces or simplifies,” said Sharma.

Niren Srivastava, Group CHRO, Motilal Oswal Financial Services, said organisations need to address the causes of pressure rather than rely only on additional programmes. “The most effective way is to fix the causes, not just treat the symptoms. That means prioritising, removing low-value work, having the right spans, and ensuring leaders showcase sustainable ways of working. Wellbeing and meaningful manager support must go hand-in-hand with ownership and performance.”

Jalan also emphasised that counselling and Employee Assistance Programmes address only part of the problem. Organisations must examine team sizes, priorities, resources and decision-making authority, while leaders need to model sustainable working practices.

The larger lesson is that managers cannot indefinitely function as shock absorbers between leadership and employees. If organisations expect them to protect team engagement, manage change and sustain performance, the conditions under which managers themselves work have to become part of the wellbeing conversation.

Mental health at work is therefore not only about helping employees cope with pressure. It is also about asking whether the organisation has designed managerial roles in a way that makes sustained performance possible without making personal wellbeing the hidden cost.

data.title: Immutable Holdings and Jorge Masvidal's Gamebred Fighting Championship (FC) Enter Into Definitive Agreement for Proposed Reverse Takeover Transaction and Listing on the TSXV
data.description:
Not for distribution to U.S. news wire services or for dissemination in the United States

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / October 9, 2026 / Immutable Holdings Inc. (CBOE:HOLD) ("Immutable" or the "Corporation") is pleased to announce that it has entered into an acquisition agreement (the "Definitive Agreement") with Gamebred FC, LLC. ("Gamebred"), which outlines the terms and conditions pursuant to which the parties will complete an arm's length transaction that will result in the reverse take-over of Immutable by Gamebred (the "Proposed Transaction") to ultimately form the resulting issuer (the "Resulting Issuer"). It is intended that the Proposed Transaction will constitute a "reverse take-over" of Immutable under the policies of CBOE Canada ("Cboe") and following completion of the Proposed Transaction, the Resulting Issuer will carry on the business currently carried on by Gamebred. It is also intended that Immutable will delist its subordinate voting shares from Cboe and the Resulting Issuer will obtain a listing on the TSX Venture Exchange ("TSXV"), subject to receipt of all required regulatory approvals.

Proposed Transaction Summary

Pursuant to the terms of the Definitive Agreement, the Proposed Transaction will be effected through a three-cornered merger (the "Merger") involving a newly incorporated Florida subsidiary of Immutable ("Newco"), whereby Newco will merge with and into Gamebred under the Florida Business Corporation Act, with Gamebred surviving the merger as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Immutable. Following completion of the Proposed Transaction, Immutable is expected to continue as the Resulting Issuer and carry on the business currently conducted by Gamebred.

There are currently an aggregate of 32,583,077 subordinate voting shares of Immutable ("SV Shares") and 65,508 multiple voting shares of Immutable ("MV Shares" and together with the SV Shares, the "Immutable Shares") issued and outstanding, as well as 4,166,100 stock options of Immutable. As a result of the Merger, the holders of the issued and outstanding shares of Gamebred ("Gamebred Shares") will receive shares of the Resulting Issuer ("Resulting Issuer Shares") in exchange for their Gamebred Shares. The aggregate consideration payable to holders of Gamebred Shares will consist of 312,500,000 Resulting Issuer Shares, subject to adjustments, with the exact number of Resulting Issuer Shares issuable per Gamebred Share determined by dividing 312,500,000 by the number of Gamebred Shares issued and outstanding on a fully diluted basis immediately prior to closing, excluding securities issued pursuant to the Concurrent Financing (as defined below) (the "Share Exchange Ratio").

Based on the number of Immutable Shares currently outstanding and the issuance of 312,500,000 Resulting Issuer Shares to the holders of Gamebred Shares pursuant to the Proposed Transaction, existing shareholders of Immutable are expected to hold approximately 23.9% of the Resulting Issuer Shares and former shareholders of Gamebred are expected to hold approximately 76.1% of the Resulting Issuer Shares immediately following completion of the Proposed Transaction, in each case prior to giving effect to the Concurrent Financing and subject to any adjustments contemplated by the Definitive Agreement. Accordingly, the foregoing ownership percentages are estimates and may change prior to closing.

At closing, all outstanding Gamebred Shares will be exchanged for Resulting Issuer Shares. Outstanding stock options of Immutable will remain outstanding following closing with no change to their existing terms.

In connection with the Proposed Transaction, Immutable intends to change its name to a name designated by Gamebred, subject to regulatory approval and the completion of all required corporate procedures.

Bridge Loan

In connection with the execution of the Definitive Agreement, the Corporation advanced a bridge loan in the principal amount of US$1,000,000 to Gamebred pursuant to the terms of a secured promissory note entered into between the Corporation and Gamebred (the "Bridge Loan"). The Bridge Loan is secured by a general security agreement granting a security interest in all of the personal property, assets and undertakings of Gamebred, as well as unlimited joint and several personal guarantees from the principal shareholders of Gamebred. The Bridge Loan bears interest at a rate of equal to Daily Simple SOFR plus 6.0% per annum, calculated daily. The Bridge Loan matures on December 31, 2026.

data.title: China adds 10.52 million urban jobs in Jan-Sept, to roll out services jobs policy
data.description:
China added 10.52 million urban jobs in the first nine months of the year, meeting 87.7% of its annual target, the labour ministry said on Saturday.

The ministry is also planning new measures to boost hiring in the services sector.

The surveyed urban unemployment rate averaged 5.2% from January to August, and employment remained "generally stable," officials from the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security told a State Council Information Office press conference.

The ministry will work with other departments on a policy document to promote employment through services sector development, enabling services to better act as the main channel for absorbing jobs, Vice Minister and spokesperson Li Zhong said.

Beijing will also work to keep employment steady in labour-intensive industries and look for new job opportunities in emerging and future industries, he added.

As of end-September, 1.079 billion people were enrolled in basic pension insurance. Unemployment insurance covered 251 million people and work-injury insurance covered 327 million.

The three social insurance funds had a combined balance of 11.2 trillion yuan ($1.67 trillion).

data.title: Asahi Kasei Wins FDA Approval For HOVILPRI To Treat Drug-Resistant HSV In Immunocompromised Adults
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - Asahi Kasei Therapeutics, the specialty pharmaceutical arm of Japan's Asahi Kasei Corporation (AHKSF, 3407.T), secured U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for HOVILPRI (pritelivir) 100 mg tablets, marking a significant advance in the treatment of difficult-to-manage herpes simplex virus (HSV) infections in immunocompromised adults.

The newly approved therapy is indicated for the treatment of mucocutaneous lesions caused by HSV infections that are refractory, with or without documented resistance, to standard antiviral treatments including acyclovir, valacyclovir, and famciclovir. HOVILPRI is a first-in-class helicase-primase inhibitor developed by AiCuris Anti-infective Cures AG, which is now part of Asahi Kasei Therapeutics.

The FDA approval was supported by data from the pivotal Phase 3 PRIOH-1 Part C trial, a randomized, open-label, comparator-controlled study involving immunocompromised adults with treatment-refractory HSV infections. The study demonstrated the superiority of pritelivir over existing therapies in patients whose infections were resistant or unresponsive to currently available antiviral medications.

HSV infections are generally mild or asymptomatic in healthy individuals. However, people with weakened immune systems, including organ and stem cell transplant recipients, people living with HIV, and patients with cancer or autoimmune diseases, can experience more frequent, severe, and persistent infections. Drug-resistant HSV can lead to prolonged and difficult-to-treat mucocutaneous lesions, creating a significant unmet medical need.

Asahi Kasei Therapeutics expects HOVILPRI to become commercially available in the United States before the end of 2026, offering physicians a new tool to address a challenging patient population with limited treatment alternatives.

AHKSF closed Friday's regular trading at $10.30 up $0.26 or 2.62%.

Flagship PlantBrain platform, backed by a strategic investment from Chemelex, debuts as a standalone public company serving large-scale manufacturing, energy, and infrastructure operators globally

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 9, 2026) - Algo8 AI Inc. (CSE: AIOS) ("Algo8" or the "Company"), the Industrial Artificial Intelligence company behind the PlantBrain™ platform and more than 80 successful deployments across the steel, tire, automotive, and energy sectors, is pleased to announce that has received final approval to list its common shares (the "Shares") on the Canadian Securities Exchange ("CSE"). The Shares are expected to begin trading on the CSE on or about October 13, 2026 under the symbol "AIOS" and CUSIP/ISIN: 016917106/CA0169171067.

The listing marks Algo8's debut as a standalone public company and brings one of Canada's most advanced Industrial AI platforms to the public markets.

Listing Details

The listing follows the closing, on October 6, 2026, of the previously announced plan of arrangement (the "Arrangement"), under which the Company acquired the Algo8 business. For further information on the listing and the business of Algo8, please refer to the listing statement in the form of CSE Form 2A dated effective September 30, 2026 (the "Listing Statement") on its SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca.

Pursuant to the Arrangement, Shares issued to all former Algo8 Industrial AI Inc. shareholders and finders in connection with the Arrangement are subject to restrictions on transfer, representing approximately 66.06% of the issued and outstanding Shares. Founders, management and advisors of Algo8 are restricted from trading for the first 12 months after listing and Shares are released in stages through the 36-month anniversary of the trading date. Shares issued to Chemelex and finders in connection with the Arrangement are subject to a shorter lock-up period, with 50% released six months after the trading date and the remaining 50% at 12 months. Full details are set out in the Listing Statement.

Management Commentary

"Today is a defining milestone for Algo8 and for every shareholder who has backed this team," said Brandon Kou, President and Director of Algo8. "Algo8 arrives on the CSE as a commercial business, with more than 80 deployments behind it, Chemelex as a strategic investor and a founder group that has locked in for years. Industrial operators are no longer asking whether to adopt AI; they are asking who can make it work on the plant floor. We are excited to be one of the first early-stage Industrial AI companies that investors can access through the public markets. Our focus from here is disciplined execution: expanding within the customers we already serve, winning new operators and building a shareholder base that understands the scale of this opportunity."

Mr. Kou is a seasoned public market executive and investor. He previously served as Chief Executive Officer of publicly traded Leef Brands and held senior leadership positions at Steve Nash Enterprises, and began his career in investment banking at Houlihan Lokey.

"We founded Algo8 in 2018 on a simple belief: the digital economy has operating systems for information, but the industrial world has lacked an intelligence layer that understands the plant, predicts what comes next and acts on it," said Nandan Mishra, Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Algo8. "PlantBrain™ is that layer. It connects the systems our customers already run and turns their data into decisions and actions across scheduling, maintenance, quality, energy and throughput. Listing on the CSE gives us the visibility and the access to capital to take what is already working in some of the world's most demanding plants to operators around the globe. I want to thank our customers, our team and our shareholders for getting us here."

Mr. Mishra is an engineer by training from the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur who began his career at Google Maps. Since co-founding Algo8 in 2018, he has led its growth into an Industrial AI platform company serving manufacturing, energy and process industries across multiple continents.

Industrial AI at Commercial Scale

Algo8 enters the public markets with a commercial track record:

  • More than 80 successful PlantBrain™ deployments across the steel, tire, automotive, and energy sectors globally.
  • A strategic investment of $2.79 million from Chemelex LLC
  • A Phase 1 multi-plant deployment with a global tire manufacturer, under an initial contract of approximately $4.0 million plus potential recurring support.
  • A global footprint, with customer relationships and pipeline across North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia.

Unlike point solutions that address a single operational metric, Algo8's Industrial AI Operating System connects the operational and business systems customers already run. It combines industrial context with generative, agentic, predictive, and physical AI to turn industrial data into decisions and actions. Engagements run from an initial diagnostic through deployment and ongoing support, and customer relationships have consistently expanded from a first deployment into multi-site, multi-use-case programs.

The CSE listing is the next step in Algo8's strategy to scale its Industrial AI platform. The Company intends to deepen its work with existing customers, add new large-scale operators in North America and internationally, and continue advancing the platform toward progressively more autonomous operations.

Algo8 is led by Mr. Mishra, Co-Founder and Chief Technology Officer Himanshu Singh, a fellow alumnus of IIT Kanpur with more than a decade applying AI to complex manufacturing and supply chain environments, and Mr. Kou. The board of directors comprises Mr. Kou, Mr. Mishra, Mr. Singh, Douglas Steinberg, an Operator in Residence at Primary Venture Partners, and Nicholas Mersch, a Portfolio Manager at Purpose Investments covering artificial intelligence across the public markets.

"Listing day is day one," added Mr. Mishra. "The work is the same as it was yesterday: make industrial operations more productive and progressively more autonomous, one plant at a time. Now we do it as a public company, with our shareholders alongside us."

Its Industrial AI Operating System, anchored by the flagship PlantBrain™ platform, connects the operational and business systems customers already run and combines industrial context with generative, agentic, predictive and physical AI to turn industrial data into decisions and actions. data.title: SlowMist CISO Speculates on Ledger Attack Path Involving Screen Recording of Seed Phrase
data.description:
SlowMist Chief Information Security Officer 23pds said that if the Ledger modification described by former Mt. Gox CEO Mark Karpelès occurred on the PCB, it would indicate a highly sophisticated attack. He outlined a possible sequence in which the seed is generated inside the secure element, the recovery phrase is shown on the screen, and a malicious module taps the screen data line, such as SPI, to record the displayed words before sending them out through LTE or eSIM.

According to Foresight News, 23pds said attackers could then obtain the recovery phrase and transfer the assets. He added that the module could be used to analyze characters shown to the user and transmit the related data after the phrase setup is completed.

Karpelès previously said he received a Ledger hardware wallet that appeared to contain a spy module. He said the device came from Malaysia, the outer shrink wrap was intact, and no anomaly was immediately visible after opening it. He said the implant was hidden where the screen’s original cushioning pad should have been and included LTE communication components, an antenna, an eSIM, and a microcontroller connected to the Ledger SPI bus.

Karpelès said the attacker may have monitored the victim’s wallet address and chosen a time to move the assets.

data.title: Patrick Collison Says Personal AI Agents Could Increase Returns for High-Quality Products
data.description:
Stripe co-founder and CEO Patrick Collison said personal AI agents could change how consumers interact with companies and may reduce the effectiveness of tactics such as coupon-based price discrimination and cross-subsidies tied to forgotten subscription cancellations. According to ChainCatcher, he argued that personal agents could make people more rational in dealings with companies and act as a structural subsidy for product quality.

Collison said the impact on the broader economy remains uncertain, including who ultimately bears the cost of these changes. He added that if consumers continue to spend significant time researching purchases, improving product quality could become a more effective corporate strategy, while product-quality information would become more important and influential.

He also said most people currently have limited ability to integrate product-quality data, but agents would create ongoing demand for such signals. Beyond helping train models, data could become more valuable as a cheaper complement to intelligence. Collison said open questions remain over whether agents will strengthen star products, increase choice fragmentation by better identifying differentiated preferences, or change demand routing and display fees driven by short attention spans.

data.title: Kalshi Research Examines Who Trades Prediction Markets
data.description:
Kalshi Research, a unit of prediction market platform Kalshi, published a report titled "Who Trades Prediction Markets?" in October 2026. According to ChainCatcher, the study examined the makeup of prediction market traders using administrative records and survey data, then compared the results with a general population sample.

The administrative data covered each direct Kalshi trader's residential ZIP code from January 2026 and was benchmarked against median household income from the U.S. Community Survey. The survey was sent in September 2026 to 2,360 accounts with the highest profit and loss across market categories excluding sports and special categories; 325 responses were completed, for a 13.8% response rate.

The report said the median income reflected by traders' residences was close to the national level, with the modal income band crossing $80,734, and only 6.3% living in ZIP codes with median income above $150,000. Among the highest profit and loss traders, 82% had never worked full time at an investment bank, hedge fund, private equity firm, or proprietary trading firm, 91% were not full-time traders, and 65% said they were largely or entirely self-taught in markets and probability. Compared with 1,005 U.S. adults, the group scored 2.42 out of 4 on the Berlin Numeracy Test versus 0.62 for the public, and 93% resisted the gambler's fallacy versus 57% of the public.
